hook_text: Four periods, four people, one crane. The teams that finish are the ones who drew the recipe first.
clip_script: A flow chart is a recipe in shapes. Oval: start. Rectangle: one step, with a verb. Cut the base. Roll the mast. Diamond: a question. Does the magnet lift ten clips? Yes goes on. No loops back: add turns, test again. Oval: end. Now order the crane. Glue the slow parts first, base, mast, arm. While they dry, wind the coil, make the winch, fit the pulley. Test the magnet on the bench, not inside the finished crane. Then assemble, wire, string. Test the whole thing: lift, move, drop, still standing? Draw it in columns, one per person, so four pairs of hands work at once. Then walk it aloud: who, with what, how long. Tick the boxes as you build. Nobody argues about what comes next.
visual_style: Whiteboard shapes appearing one by one; a column of boxes with a diamond branching and looping; three parallel columns merging into one.
mood: Organised and energising, a plan clicking into place.
pacing: Shapes, order, test, assemble, test, columns, walk, tick, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the recipe for your own build.
